records.name: Friends of Gold Star Park
records.summary: Neighbors who look after Gold Star Park, a small park on Wharton Street in South Philadelphia. They run programs for kids, families, and dog owners, and they invite new volunteers to help.
records.what_you_do: Help run the park's summer programs and its upkeep. The site does not describe volunteer tasks in detail.

schedule.text: Children's, family, and dog-owner programs run through the summer; no dates published

first_step.how: Sign up for the group's newsletter on goldstarpark.org, or message the group through its Facebook page, and ask how to volunteer
first_step.basis: The site invites new volunteers and offers a newsletter sign-up, though it publishes no meeting schedule

records.notes: The site has no dated posts. Status is probably_active only because it is a working site that describes current programs. The site's email link is hidden from automated reading, so no email is recorded. The street number 613 comes from the City list, not the group's site. Tai chi, a school recess, and a bocce league use the park; they are not confirmed as the group's own programs.

records.name: Friends of Gorgas Park
records.summary: Neighbors who care for Gorgas Park in Roxborough. They put on park concerts and family events, and they hold spring planting and cleanup days.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a spring planting or cleanup day, help at a family event or concert, or donate to the park.

schedule.text: Spring planting and cleanup days, and summer concerts; dates are posted each season

cost.text: No admission or membership fee listed; the site has a donate page

first_step.how: Watch the Volunteer page on gorgaspark.com for the next spring planting or cleanup day, and register through the link there
first_step.basis: Planting and cleanup days are open to volunteers who sign up on the group's site

records.notes: The site has a contact form only, with no published email, so none is recorded. The City list's email (pprstewardship@phila.gov) is the Parks office, not the group. The newest dated item is a 2026 season page dated 2026-06-23. Posts are seasonal, and there is no regular meeting schedule.

records.name: SEAMAAC Growing Home Gardens
records.summary: Community gardens on Emily and Mercy Streets in South Philadelphia, run by SEAMAAC, an immigrant and refugee services nonprofit, with the Neighborhood Gardens Trust. Mostly immigrant and refugee gardeners grow vegetables and familiar foods here. We could not confirm current activity.
records.what_you_do: Rent a garden plot and grow food. Ask the gardens office about open plots and the yearly fee before you visit.

schedule.text: Plots are worked through the growing season; no meeting or work-day schedule is published

first_step.how: Email gardens@seamaac.org or call (347) 719-1488 to ask about open plots and the yearly fee
first_step.basis: The gardens exist to serve newly arrived immigrants and refugees and publish a contact, but the page gives no joining steps

records.notes: The newest dated item I could place is an October 2020 groundbreaking report, seen in a search result only (the page was not opened). The SEAMAAC gardens page still describes plans for 2021 and its footer says 2021, so activity is probably more than two years old. The Neighborhood Gardens Trust still lists the gardens and gives gardens@seamaac.org and (347) 719-1488. The City list email (info@seamaac-local) is an internal placeholder domain used by SEAMAAC's own site, so it is not recorded. A news snippet gave a $25 yearly fee, but its date is unclear, so no cost is recorded. Call before visiting.

records.name: Friends of Harrowgate Park
records.summary: Neighbors who look after Harrowgate Park in Kensington. They put on park events such as a movie night and a winter tree lighting, and they take part in neighborhood art projects.
records.what_you_do: Come to park events, donate through the site, or ask how to help with the next event. The site does not describe volunteer tasks.

schedule.text: Upcoming events: a movie night on October 16, 2026 (activities from 4 pm, movie at 6 pm) and a tree lighting on December 11, 2026 (6 to 8 pm)

first_step.how: Come to the Movie Night on October 16, 2026 at Harrowgate Park, 3455 Kensington Ave, from 4 pm, and ask a Friends member how to help
first_step.basis: Public events on set dates, but the site does not explain how to join the group itself

records.notes: The City list's www address has a certificate name mismatch, so the bare harrowgatepark.com domain was used. The City list email (Friendsofharrowgatepark@gmail.com) differs from the site's (FriendsOfHarrowgate@gmail.com); confirm before use. The phone number is as shown on the site and may be the recreation center's line. The Instagram posts show no year, so the 2026 date comes from the 2026 event listings. The Fall Festival on October 10, 2026 is run by Harrowgate Civic, a separate group.

records.name: Friends of Hawthorne Park
records.summary: A park group listed by Parks and Recreation for Hawthorne Park, a small park in South Philadelphia near 12th and Catharine Streets. We could not reach its website or find recent news, so what it does now is unconfirmed.

first_step.how: Email Parks and Recreation's stewardship office (pprstewardship@phila.gov) and ask to be connected with this Friends group

records.notes: The City layer gives hawthornepark.org as the website. Both the www and bare domains have an expired security certificate, so the site could not be read, and no website is recorded. The City's French-language list shows no website for Parc Hawthorne. Web searches found no group pages. The City layer gives 750 S 12th St, while the park itself is near 12th and Catharine. The Hawthorne Empowerment Coalition appears in search results as a source for the park's design, but nothing found confirms it runs this group. No dated sign of life found.

records.name: Historic Rittenhousetown
records.summary: A historic village in the Wissahickon area with a 1707 homestead, several historic houses, an arboretum, and a small museum. Visitors take tours, and volunteers and members help keep the site going.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer on site, become a member, take a Saturday tour, or come to the free Second Saturday museum visits.

schedule.text: Tours on Saturdays from Memorial Day through Labor Day, 12 to 3 pm, starting on the hour. Free Second Saturday museum visits. Fall Fest from 5 to 8 pm (the event date is not on the page)

cost.text: Tours $10 a person (children under 8 free); Second Saturday museum visits are free; Fall Fest is pay what you can

first_step.how: Take a Saturday tour from 12 to 3 pm ($10 a person), then ask about volunteering or membership through the Volunteer page on rittenhousetown.org
first_step.basis: Tours and museum visits are open to the public, and the site lists volunteer and membership options

records.notes: This is a historic village and museum rather than a neighborhood Friends group. It is published because it runs volunteer and membership programs. The City list address (6014 Wissahickon Ave) differs from the site's 208 Lincoln Drive, and this record uses the site's address. The Fall Fest post is dated September 25, 2026, and its text gives no event date.

records.name: Friends of Howell Park
records.summary: A park group for Howell Park on Greene Street. It joined the City's Park Friends network in 2019, and we found no newer sign of life.

first_step.how: Email Parks and Recreation's stewardship office (pprstewardship@phila.gov) and ask to be connected with this Friends group

records.notes: The City list gives fojsp.org as this group's website, but fojsp.org belongs to Friends of Jefferson Square Park (300 Washington Ave), so it is not used here. No website for this group was found. Its only dated evidence is the City's March 7, 2019 welcome to the Park Friends network, so the status is dormant. The group is still on the City's current list, so it may be active without a web presence. A later pass should look for a current contact.

records.name: Hunting Park United
records.summary: A neighborhood group in Hunting Park that cleans and greens the park, plants trees and gardens, and runs family fitness days and senior programs.
records.what_you_do: Join a park cleanup, a tree or garden planting, a fitness or family day, or a senior activity. Call or stop by the office to ask about the next event.

schedule.text: Cleanups, planting, fitness, and family events through the year. The latest listed events were in August and September 2026. Office hours: Monday to Friday 9 am to 5 pm, Saturday 10 am to 2 pm

first_step.how: Call 267-800-3894, or visit 1101 W Hunting Park Ave during office hours, and ask about the next cleanup or fitness day
first_step.basis: Events are open to the public and the office takes calls, but the site does not describe formal membership steps

records.notes: The site hides its email from automated reading. The City list shows huntingparkunited@aol.com, but that address is not on the group's site, so it is not recorded; confirm by phone. The homepage says the group does community gardening, but no garden or orchard address is given.

records.name: Hunting Park Community Garden & Orchard
records.summary: A community garden and orchard in Hunting Park, listed by Parks and Recreation as a Friends group. We could not find its own website or any recent news.

first_step.how: Email Parks and Recreation's stewardship office (pprstewardship@phila.gov) and ask to be connected with this Friends group

records.notes: The City's French list calls it 'Jardin communautaire du parc de chasse' and shows no website. Hunting Park United's site mentions community gardening but gives no garden address, so this record is not linked to it. Not searched (search budget spent on other groups).

records.name: Friends of Inn Yard Park
records.summary: A park group for Inn Yard Park on Ridge Avenue in Northwest Philadelphia. We could not find a website or recent news for it.

first_step.how: Email Parks and Recreation's stewardship office (pprstewardship@phila.gov) and ask to be connected with this Friends group

records.notes: Neither the City layer nor the City's French list shows a website. Not searched, because the search budget went to other groups in this batch. A later pass should search for it.

records.name: Friends of Jefferson Square Park
records.summary: Neighbors who look after Jefferson Square Park on Washington Avenue in Pennsport. They hold a park cleanup on the second Saturday of the month and welcome ideas for the park.
records.what_you_do: Join a Saturday cleanup, come to park events such as the October 13, 2026 ribbon cutting for the Washington Avenue connector, or share ideas for the park.

schedule.text: Park cleanups on the second Saturday of the month, 9 to 11 am. Listed dates: October 10, 2026 and November 14, 2026

cost.text: No fee listed; the group asks for donations

first_step.how: Come to the Saturday cleanup on October 10, 2026, 9 to 11 am, at 300 Washington Ave, or use the Contact Us page on fojsp.org to ask how to join
first_step.basis: Cleanups are announced publicly and anyone can come, but the site does not describe a welcome for newcomers

records.notes: The City list's website was a Facebook group, which was not used as the website. The group's own site is fojsp.org. The City's French list gives jeffersonsquarepark.org, which redirects to an unrelated domain (rajabandothyper.com). That redirect was not followed. The City list's Friends of Howell Park record also points to fojsp.org; see that record. I opened the Facebook group link once to check that it loads and took no facts from it.

records.name: Collazo Friends & Team NAS
records.summary: A friends group for Jose Manuel Collazo Park on Mascher Street in North Philadelphia. We could not find its own website or recent news.

first_step.how: Email Parks and Recreation's stewardship office (pprstewardship@phila.gov) and ask to be connected with this Friends group

records.notes: No website on the City list, and the City's French list does not show this group. The 'Team NAS' part of the name could not be identified from the City list. Not searched (search budget spent on other groups).

records.name: Friends of Julian Abele Park
records.summary: A nonprofit group for Julian Abele Park, a small park on 22nd Street in Southwest Center City. Members meet about eight times a year, and the group runs a summer concert series.
records.what_you_do: Join as a general member for $20 a year, attend the group's meetings, or come to the summer concerts. Voting members must be 18 or older and meet attendance or service rules.

schedule.text: Meets about eight times a year, usually the first Tuesday of the month at 7 pm at SOSNA, 1901 Christian Street. Exact dates are not listed. Summer concerts run on Tuesdays, 6 to 8 pm, in 2026

cost.text: $20 a year in dues for general membership; no concert fee is listed

first_step.how: Pay the $20 yearly dues to join as a general member, then come to a meeting, usually the first Tuesday of the month at 7 pm at SOSNA, 1901 Christian Street. Check the group's contact page for the next date
first_step.basis: Joining costs $20 a year, and the site does not say whether meetings are open to non-members

records.notes: The City list gives friendsofjulianabele@gmail.com, which the group's site does not show, so it is not recorded. The contact page has only a mailing list sign-up form. The 2026 concert series has no posting date on the page; the 2026-09 date reflects the page's statement that the series runs into September. The site's other dated posts are from 2015 and 2016. The City list address (923 S 22nd St) is used; the site describes the park as 22nd Street between Montrose and Carpenter Streets.

records.name: Friends of June 5th Memorial Park
records.summary: A friends group for June 5th Memorial Park at 2140 Market Street. The only dated sign of life we found is a 2019 City welcome to the Park Friends network.

first_step.how: Email Parks and Recreation's stewardship office (pprstewardship@phila.gov) and ask to be connected with this Friends group

records.notes: No website was found. The status is dormant only because the newest dated item found is the City's March 2019 welcome. The group is still on the City's current list, so it may be active without a web presence. Not searched (search budget spent on other groups). A later pass should recheck.
